name: Tipped Minimum Wage
description: Amendments to employer gratuity allowances and hourly wage rules for tipped workers.
summary: The contested item was the future of Chicago's One Fair Wage phase-out of the tipped subminimum wage. SO2025-0017549, amending Municipal Code Section 6-105-030 on employer gratuity allowances, was introduced 2025-05-21 and passed City Council 30 Yea / 18 Nay on 2026-03-18, after testimony both opposing changes to the ordinance and criticizing its effects on businesses [5][8]. A follow-up measure, SO2026-0024043, modifying timelines for employer allowance minimums, was introduced 2026-03-18 and taken up by the Committee on Workforce Development on 2026-05-12. The negotiated substitute, per Alderman Burnett, freezes the tip credit wage at 24% for two years, with a longer four-year ramp-up for small businesses, phasing out until 2030 [7][4][6]. Industry representatives said the substitute was not ideal but more workable than the existing phase-out, while One Fair Wage advocates said they could live with it but urged enforcement against wage theft [1][4][6]. The committee recommended do pass by unanimous voice vote [3][9][12], and City Council passed SO2026-0024043 49 Yea / 1 Nay on 2026-05-20, with speakers describing it as a compromise or 'pause' while reaffirming a commitment to eventual full minimum wage for tipped workers [2]. Still open are implementation of the freeze and ramp-up timeline, enforcement of wage-theft claims, and whether the promised eventual wage increase for tipped workers will occur [2][7].
one_line: Council passed SO2026-0024043 (49-1) freezing the 24% tip credit through 2028, phasing out by 2030; enforcement details remain open.
